```{python}
#| label: setup
import json

import pandas as pd

from acme_eval.claims import claim

metrics = pd.read_csv("outputs/metrics.csv")
summary = json.loads(open("outputs/summary.json").read())
value = metrics.pivot(index="metric", columns="version", values="value")
best = summary["best_version"]
versions = [release["version"] for release in summary["releases"]]
claim(best == value.loc["roc_auc"].idxmax(), "The release called best has the highest ROC AUC.")
claim(value.loc["lift_top10", best] > 1,
      "The best release finds more subscribers per call than calling at random.")


def percent(share: float, digits: int = 1) -> str:
    """A share between 0 and 1, as a percentage."""
    return f"{100 * share:.{digits}f}%"
```

Of releases `{python} versions[0]` to `{python} versions[-1]` of the contact-ranking model,
**`{python} best`** ranks best: calling the top `{python} percent(summary["top_share"], 0)`
of its list reaches `{python} percent(value.loc["recall_top10", best])` of the subscribers
among `{python} f"{summary['test_rows']:,}"` held-out contacts,
`{python} f"{value.loc['lift_top10', best]:.1f}"` times as many per call as calling at
random. Acme Signals is a fictional company, made up for teaching; the bank data are real
and public, and every number on this site is computed from them.
